target.title: fix(agents): web_fetch leaves body open after provider fallback
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `web_fetch` could leave an upstream response body open when a non-OK (or extraction-failed) response was abandoned after a successful provider fallback return. `finally` only called `release()`; the unread (or abandoned) body was never cancelled.

## Why This Change Was Made

Before returning a provider-fallback payload that abandons the direct fetch response, cancel the response body best-effort (`body?.cancel().catch(...)`), matching the cancel-before-release campaign used elsewhere in core. Covers both the non-OK early-return path and the readability-disabled HTML fallback return path.

## User Impact

**Before:** Successful provider fallback after a non-OK upstream (or after skipping local HTML extraction) could retain an abandoned response stream until GC.

**After:** The abandoned upstream body is cancelled before returning the fallback payload; dispatcher release still runs in `finally`.

## Evidence

### Proof (exit 0)

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/web-fetch.provider-fallback.test.ts -t "cancels an unread non-OK|cancels the response body when readability" --reporter=verbose
```

```text
stdout | ... > cancels an unread non-OK response body when provider fallback succeeds
[web-fetch non-ok fallback cancel proof] cancelled=true extractor=custom-provider

stdout | ... > cancels the response body when readability-disabled fallback succeeds
[web-fetch readability-off fallback cancel proof] cancel_invoked=true extractor=custom-provider

 ✓ |agents-core| ... > cancels an unread non-OK response body when provider fallback succeeds 232ms
 ✓ |agents-core| ... > cancels the response body when readability-disabled fallback succeeds 11ms
 ✓ |agents-tools| ... > cancels an unread non-OK response body when provider fallback succeeds 375ms
 ✓ |agents-tools| ... > cancels the response body when readability-disabled fallback succeeds 18ms

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  4 passed | 10 skipped (14)
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Non-OK and readability-disabled HTML upstream bodies are cancelled when provider fallback succeeds and returns early.
- **Canonical reachability path:** `createWebFetchTool` → fetch → `maybeFetchProviderWebFetchPayload` success → `cancelUnreadWebFetchBody(res)` → return payload → `release()`.
- **Boundary crossed:** Abandoned upstream HTTP body stream → `body.cancel()` before fallback return (non-OK unread path + readability-off path).
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Local `cancelUnreadWebFetchBody` uses `body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` (same best-effort pattern as other cancel-unread helpers).
- **Observed result after fix:** `cancelled=true` (non-OK) and `cancel_invoked=true` (readability-off) with `extractor=custom-provider` (see proof log).
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix

- [x] AI-assisted (Cursor)
- [x] I understand what the code does
- [x] Change is focused and does not mix unrelated concerns

target.title: fix(qa-lab): cancel unread response body on HTTP error + fix(vertex-adc): guard JSON.parse
target.body:
## Summary

**What changed**: Two fixes in this PR.

1. **qa-lab: cancel unread response body on HTTP error** — Add `response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before throwing on non-2xx responses in `getJson`/`getJsonNoStore` so the connection is released back to the pool.
2. **vertex-adc: guard JSON.parse against malformed credential files** — Wrap `JSON.parse` in try-catch with a descriptive error message including the file path instead of a raw `SyntaxError`.

**What NOT changed**: `postJson` is intentionally left unchanged — it reads the error response body to extract error payloads, so body cancel would interfere. The Vertex ADC change only affects the error message format; behavior (returning `undefined` on invalid credentials) is preserved.

Fixes #109985

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**:
- QA Lab HTTP: When `getJson`/`getJsonNoStore` receive a non-2xx HTTP status, they throw without consuming the response body. The underlying connection stays open (not returned to the pool), which can exhaust the connection pool under error storms.
- Vertex ADC: A malformed credential file at `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` causes a raw `SyntaxError` from `JSON.parse`, giving users no indication of which file is broken.

**Root Cause**:
- QA Lab HTTP: `getJson`/`getJsonNoStore` call `response.json()` only on success. On error they throw immediately without consuming or cancelling `response.body`. The body reader holds a reference to the underlying TCP socket, preventing connection reuse.
- Vertex ADC: `readGoogleAdcCredentials` calls `JSON.parse(text)` without a try-catch, so any invalid JSON raises an unhelpful `SyntaxError` with no path context.

**Solution**:
- QA Lab HTTP: Insert `response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before the `throw` in both `getJson` and `getJsonNoStore`. Optional chaining handles null body; `.catch()` suppresses cancellation rejections.
- Vertex ADC: Wrap `JSON.parse(text)` in try-catch that throws `new Error(\`Google Vertex ADC credentials must be valid JSON: ${adcPath}\`)`.

## Evidence

### Fix 1: QA Lab HTTP body cancel

**Real environment tested**:
Node.js 22, vitest 4.1.10, Linux 6.17.0-40-generic

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
npx vitest run extensions/qa-lab/web/src/http.evidence.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```
 ✓ |extension-qa| http.evidence.test.ts > QA Lab HTTP body cancel on HTTP error > getJson 400: body cancelled 66ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| http.evidence.test.ts > QA Lab HTTP body cancel on HTTP error > getJson 403: body cancelled 1ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| http.evidence.test.ts > QA Lab HTTP body cancel on HTTP error > getJson 500: body cancelled 1ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| http.evidence.test.ts > QA Lab HTTP body cancel on HTTP error > getJsonNoStore 429: body cancelled 0ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| http.evidence.test.ts > QA Lab HTTP body cancel on HTTP error > getJsonNoStore 503: body cancelled 1ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| http.evidence.test.ts > QA Lab HTTP body cancel on HTTP error > Null body: safe (no error on missing body) 0ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| http.evidence.test.ts > QA Lab HTTP body cancel on HTTP error > Cancel rejection: suppressed 1ms
```

**Observed result after the fix**:
All non-2xx paths call `response.body?.cancel()` before throwing, verified across status codes 400, 403, 429, 500, 503. Null body and cancellation rejection edge cases are also handled.

**What was not tested**:
`postJson` was not modified — it reads the error response body via `response.json()` to extract an error payload, so body cancel would interfere.

### Fix 2: Vertex ADC JSON.parse guard

**Real environment tested**:
Node.js 22, vitest 4.1.10, Linux 6.17.0-40-generic

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
npx vitest run extensions/google/vertex-adc.evidence.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```
 ✓ |extension-providers| vertex-adc.evidence.test.ts > Vertex ADC JSON.parse guard (PR #109985) > demonstrates the JSON.parse try-catch improvement 96ms
 ✓ |extension-providers| vertex-adc.evidence.test.ts > Vertex ADC JSON.parse guard (PR #109985) > gracefully handles malformed ADC file via config resolver 3ms
```

**Observed result after the fix**:
Malformed JSON at `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` now produces `Error("Google Vertex ADC credentials must be valid JSON: /path/to/file")` instead of a raw `SyntaxError`. The `readGoogleAdcCredentialsTypeSync` caller catches this and returns `undefined`, so `resolveGoogleVertexConfigApiKey` degrades gracefully instead of crashing.

**What was not tested**:
The fix is in `readGoogleAdcCredentials` which is called from two paths: (a) `readGoogleAdcCredentialsTypeSync` used by `hasGoogleVertexAuthorizedUserAdcSync`, and (b) `resolveGoogleVertexAuthorizedUserHeaders`. Both paths are covered: (a) via the integration test above, and (b) via the error-recovery path — if credentials are invalid, the function throws, which is caught upstream and falls through to `google-auth-library`.

## Tests and validation

### Evidence tests

Both evidence test suites pass at exact HEAD `cab77b1ef899c5734eb4a686873ed880f075cd14`:

```
$ npx vitest run extensions/qa-lab/web/src/http.evidence.test.ts extensions/google/vertex-adc.evidence.test.ts --reporter=verbose

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  9 passed (9)
```

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [ ] I have updated relevant documentation
- [ ] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary
- merge-risk: auth-provider — both fixes add defensive guards without changing auth flow or error semantics. The Vertex ADC fix wraps an existing error path in a clearer message; the QA Lab fix adds body cleanup before existing throws. No credential path, token exchange, or provider selection logic is altered.

## Real Module Test Evidence

```
 ✓ |extension-qa| ../../extensions/qa-lab/web/src/http.test.ts > QA Lab dashboard HTTP > gives every API request a fresh 30 second deadline 70ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| ../../extensions/qa-lab/web/src/http.test.ts > QA Lab dashboard HTTP > rejects a stalled request when its deadline aborts 2ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
```
